summary: Morehouse Parish state fire tower, Fire Tower 4, described in a 1939 survey as about 100 ft of steel with a glass cab; listed as torn down and removed; no current site description.

facts.design: Steel structure about 100 feet high with a glass-enclosed platform on top (1939 Coast and Geodetic Survey description)
facts.status_note: Wikipedia list says torn down; the Forest Lookouts site says removed; no removal date given

events.note: Described in a Coast and Geodetic Survey station record as a Louisiana state fire tower, designation Fire Tower 4

evidence.supports: described as a Louisiana state fire tower
evidence.quote: OBSERVED CENTER OF LOUISIANA STATE FIRE TOWER.

evidence.supports: tower is about 12 miles north of Bastrop

evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1939 (FBQ)

evidence.supports: steel structure about 100 feet high with glass-enclosed platform on top
evidence.quote: STEEL STRUCTURE ABOUT 100 FEET HIGH WITH GLASS ENCLOSED PLATFORM ATOP.

evidence.supports: surveyors observed the tower from five triangulation stations, including Beekman
evidence.quote: OBSERVED UPON FROM TRIANGULATION STATION RAWLS, WHITE, BEEKMAN, STEVENS AND CUTOVER.

evidence.supports: in 1915 funds for fire protection work allowed hiring lookout watchmen
evidence.quote: In 1915 funds were directed for fire protection work allowing the hiring of lookout watchmen or patrolmen.
By 1943 thirty-nine fire towers had been built and by 1950 the number had increased to fifty-six.

Forest Lookouts site records the tower as removed
list compilers could not view the site on Street View or older aerial imagery
evidence.quote: Unable to view on street view or older aerial imagery.

corrections.proposed: Louisiana state fire tower (no agency named in the sources)
corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page gives 22N-6E-Sec.4 as a township, range and section location, not an agency. The 1939 survey record calls the tower a Louisiana state fire tower and names no agency.

sources.title: List of fire lookout towers in Louisiana

notes_for_editor: The 1939 Coast and Geodetic Survey text is only available as reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the NGS datasheet itself was not opened. Build date, staffing and fires were not found in two searches, so the story leaves them out. The brief's agency value is a township-range-section code and is corrected above. Brief height 30.5 m matches the survey's 'about 100 feet'. Brief coordinates match Wikipedia. No agency is given in facts because no source names one. No access level is recorded because no source says whether the site is public.
